sag_decision.question: the 7.1 px sag on bay 2
sag_decision.why_the_old_number_is_wrong: null_verdict() charges each bay's MAXIMUM sag (reached around frame 1165) at the camera's CLOSEST approach (frame 888 for bay 2, 3.53 m). Those two never coincide: at 888 the sag is still small, and by the time it is 16 mm the camera is 20-600 m away. The pixel figure is a product of two numbers taken from different frames.
sag_decision.re_measured: per shard, per frame, projected through the ONER camera's own animated transform, over every frame from release (860) to 2978, counting only shards actually inside the frame
sag_decision.creep_vs_ring_honesty: the module reports RING, but only just: drift over the window 18.24 mm against ring peak-to-peak 11.78 mm, and the classifier calls CREEP only above 2.0x. The margin is 1.55x, not comfortable.
sag_decision.decision: ACCEPT, buy nothing. (1) The bay the decision was taken on is not the worst bay: measured jointly, bay 2 is 1.12 px and bay 7 is 3.20 px. (2) 1.12 px meets the criterion's own 1 px to within 12 %. (3) Solver iterations were priced and refused: (8,60) ran 2,205 s on 60 frames without finishing against ~240 s at 24, i.e. >=9x on a bake that already takes 4.5 h locally for 1,657 frames - >=40 h to move 3.2 px to maybe 1 px. (4) Decisive: the sag is a 20 mm artefact on a wall whose primary result is wrong by two orders of magnitude (see aperture_calibration). Any threshold change that opens the wall changes the sag too, so buying it now buys it twice.

declared.source: mullion_intact.breach_state() and the beat sheet's camera anchor

aperture_calibration.verdict: THE WALL DOES NOT OPEN. Against a declared 9.6 x 5.6 m aperture the sim produces 0.65 x 1.92 m of glass that actually left, and nothing at all that fell. There is no hole in the finished wound.

root_cause_of_the_missing_aperture.trajectory: raw bake, sim/tmp/breach_bake.npz, 1657 world-time frames: at +0.15 s after impact 2,127 shards are east of x=15.2; at +0.40 s, 2,839 are, and the field bulges to x=16.62 (1.65 m outboard). At +0.90 s only 438 are still east of 15.2 and the x range is back to 14.80..15.29. It stays there for the remaining 5.4 s. The wall stretches like a trampoline and springs back.
root_cause_of_the_missing_aperture.measured_cause: the shard-to-shard bond network never breaks. Of 12,756 bonded pairs, at frame 1165 92.8 % are still within 5 % of their original separation, the median separation change is 0.36 mm, and exactly ONE pair has stretched past 2x.

calibration.one_line: the median shard-to-shard bond is 34x stronger than the clamp that holds the whole pane into its frame and 8.4x Blender's own default. The pane detaches from the building before the glass breaks internally, which is why it behaves as one elastic sheet.

root_cause_of_the_missing_aperture.not_a_resample_artefact: identical on the raw 1657-frame bake and on the decimated 321-frame film table.
root_cause_of_the_missing_aperture.priced_experiment: the full bake ran locally in ~4.5 h for 1,657 frames (9.8 s/frame). A threshold sweep over a SHORT window - impact +0.5 s = 120 sim frames - costs about 20 min per point, so four points is ~80 min. That is the cheap decisive test and it has not been run.

not_done: R6 is unfulfilled: BREACH_Frame is empty. The table carries 152 MUL*/TRN* transforms (92 mullion segments, 60 transoms) and film9 contains NO object named MUL* or TRN* to bind them to. It is off camera (the breach leaves frame at 1053 and does not return until 1321) so nothing is seen to stop, but the wound is frozen mid-tremor rather than settled.

root_cause_PROVEN_by_experiment.run: blender -b --factory-startup -P sim/build_breach_sim.py -- --bake --detail 0 --frames 300 --t-bond-per-m 100 (everything else unchanged). 300 world-time frames = impact +0.646 s. 640 s of wall clock. Artefacts: sim/tmp/sw_b100.npz, sim/tmp/sw_b100.json, sim/tmp/sw_b100.log.
root_cause_PROVEN_by_experiment.verdict: the missing aperture is ONE NUMBER. At t_bond_per_m = 4000 the wall is a trampoline; at 100, with nothing else touched, the same impact opens 7.83 x 5.98 m against a declared 9.6 x 5.6 m and puts 2,592 of 3,796 shards out onto the forecourt. This is proof, not inference.
caveats: 100 is very likely TOO LOW: median net displacement is 3.97 m in 0.646 s and the peak fragment speed is 137.6 m/s, i.e. fragments leaving at ~2.4x the 16.4 m/s impactor. The correct value brackets between 100 and 4000 and wants a short sweep - the 300-frame window costs about 11 minutes a point on this box, so five points is an hour.
the 300-frame window ends with the field still in flight (median 3.97 m and moving). Where it SETTLES is not answered by this run and needs the full 1,657-frame window at the chosen threshold.

the retained bays get WORSE, exactly as predicted: bay 2's raw sag goes 16.4 mm -> 45.6 mm and creep_vs_ring flips RING -> CREEP (drift 33.6 mm over the window against a 9.7 mm ring). That is the strongest argument for not having spent anything on the 7.1 px sag: the number moves when this parameter moves.

sweep.method: identical 300-frame bakes (impact +0.646 s), ONE parameter changed, everything else default. ~12 min a point on this box. Artefacts sim/tmp/sw_b{100,400,1000}.{npz,json,log} and sim/tmp/breach_bake.npz for 4000.

table.note: SHIPPED. no hole; the wall recoils.
a CAR-SIZED hole punched through the nucleus; the tall panels stay.
the wall comes out; 2,592 shards land on the forecourt, final x 7.78..39.44.

sweep.reading: monotone and clean over 40x. The declared 9.6 x 5.6 m sits at or just below t_bond_per_m = 100; 400 gives a car-sized punch-through; 1000 and 4000 give nothing. The whole missing aperture is this one number.
sweep.caveat_on_the_metric: aperture_report() takes the bbox of the ORIGINS of shards that moved. The fracture is radially graded - most of the 3,796 shards are in the nucleus at the bottom centre - so at t=400 the 2,512 'gone' shards come from a 3.87 x 1.84 m nucleus while the tall panels above it stay put. The bbox is a fair aperture measure only once the large cells start leaving too.
sweep.unresolved_tension: aperture size and fragment energy are driven by the SAME parameter. At 100 the aperture is right but fragments travel 3.97 m median in 0.646 s at up to 137.6 m/s - about 2.4x the 16.4 m/s impactor. That smells like the car proxy: it is PASSIVE and KINEMATIC, so it has infinite effective mass and never decelerates, and the momentum it can pour into the glass is unbounded. Getting a 9.6 m aperture AND believable fragment speeds may need the car's mass modelled, not just a lower bond threshold. That is a second experiment, not a conclusion.

proposed_defect_log_entries.note: I am not permitted to edit docs/DEFECT-LOG-R2.md. These are drafted for whoever does. Next free id was stated as R2-062.

R2-062.title: The breach sim produces no aperture: the bond network never breaks and the wall recoils
R2-062.measured: Against a declared 9.6 x 5.6 m hole, sim/out/breach_film.npz ends with 458 of 3,796 shards displaced more than 0.25 m over a 0.65 x 1.92 m patch, max net displacement 0.407 m, and not one shard on the floor. The raw bake shows the field bulging 1.65 m outboard at +0.40 s and fully returning by +0.90 s, then holding for 5.4 s. 92.8 % of the 12,756 shard-to-shard bonds still sit within 5 % of their rest separation at the end and exactly ONE has stretched past 2x.
R2-062.cause: sim/build_breach_sim.py --t-bond-per-m defaults to 4000 N per metre of shared edge. Median shared edge is 21 mm, so the median breaking_threshold is 84 - 34x the 2.5 that clamps the whole pane into its frame, and 8.4x Blender's own default of 10. The pane detaches from the building before the glass parts internally, so it behaves as one elastic membrane.
R2-062.proof: one 300-frame re-bake with t_bond_per_m = 100 and nothing else changed opens 7.83 x 5.98 m and puts 2,592 of 3,796 shards east of x = 15.5, final x range 7.78..39.44 m. sim/tmp/sw_b100.{npz,json,log}; pictures at sim/out/wall_EXP_b100_end.png and sim/out/plan_EXP_b100_end.png against sim/out/wall_f1165.png.
R2-062.not_fixed: 100 is very likely too low (median fragment travel 3.97 m in 0.646 s, peak 137.6 m/s). The value brackets between 100 and 4000 and needs a sweep (~11 min a point on this box for the 300-frame window) followed by a full 1,657-frame bake at the chosen value, then resample, verify and re-apply.

R2-063.measured: render/film9.blend contains zero GW_Right_Glass* and zero GP_b*. tools/build_film_scene.py performed R3's deletion of round 1's ten panes but nothing supplied the replacement, so beat 1 and beat 2 render the showroom's east wall standing open.
R2-063.state: closed by render/film9_breach.blend, which supplies GP_b00..GP_b09 at x 14.95500..14.96650 as sim/apply_breach.py's contract requires. Anyone rendering from film9 itself is rendering an open wall.

R2-064.title: null_verdict()'s pixel pricing multiplies two numbers from different frames
R2-064.measured: build_breach_sim.null_verdict() charges each bay's MAXIMUM sag (reached about frame 1165) at the camera's CLOSEST APPROACH to that bay (frame 888 for bay 2). The two never coincide, and camera_ranges() does not check whether the bay is in frame at that key at all - it reports bay 4's closest range as 1.33 m when bay 4's nearest IN-SHOT range after the release is 24.3 m. Re-measured per shard per frame through the ONER camera's own animated transform, bay 2's worst is 1.12 px (not 10.73) and the worst retained bay is bay 7 at 3.20 px.
R2-064.consequence: the '7.1 px sag on bay 2' that has been carried as an open item is an artefact of the instrument, not of the sim.

R2-065.measured: the module docstring states that `sim/verify_breach.py --swap` renders the frame before, the frame of and the frame after the swap and diffs them. verify_breach.py contains no --swap argument and no swap function.
